record.paper_title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology, but Were Afraid to Ask
record.original_question: How do small-eigenvalue subtleties affect causal set calculations of de Sitter horizon entanglement entropy, and can the expected area laws be robustly revisited and extended to other spacetime dimensions and field theories?

evidence.quote: Specifically, causal sets approximated by 1 + 1 and 3 + 1 dimensional de Sitter spacetime were considered.
There are some subtleties involving small eigenvalues of iΔ that need to be handled with care, after which the expected area laws are obtained.
It would be interesting to revisit this problem in light of recent insights into the aforementioned subtleties. Extensions to other dimensions and field theories can also be explored.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a causal set C obtained by Poisson sprinkling into a globally hyperbolic region of (d-dimensional) de Sitter spacetime, for d = 1+1, 3+1, and more generally d ≥ 2. On C, define a free quantum scalar field via the Sorkin–Johnston (SJ) prescription: let i∆ be the (anti-self-adjoint) Pauli–Jordan operator built from the retarded minus advanced Green's functions associated with the discrete causal d'Alembertian on C, and let the SJ two-point function W_SJ be the positive part of i∆ in its spectral decomposition. For a causal "Rindler-like" wedge subregion R (e.g. one half of a symmetric slab of de Sitter bounded by a cosmological horizon), define Sorkin's spacetime entanglement entropy
   S(R) = Σ_λ λ log|λ|,
where λ runs over the generalized eigenvalues of the equation W|v⟩ = i λ ∆|v⟩ with operators restricted to R.

(a) Investigate the role of the small (near-zero) eigenvalues of i∆ in the spectral construction of W_SJ and in the generalized eigenvalue problem above. Determine a principled truncation/regularization of these small eigenvalues such that, in the continuum limit (sprinkling density ρ → ∞), the resulting S(R) for the de Sitter horizon obeys an area law
   S(R) ∼ c_d · A_horizon / ℓ_p^{d-2},
rather than a spacetime volume law, and identify the constant c_d.

(b) Establish such an area law rigorously for causal sets approximating de Sitter spacetime in dimensions d other than 1+1 and 3+1, and extend the analysis to other free field theories (e.g. massive scalars, fermions, gauge fields) on these causal sets, characterizing how the small-eigenvalue subtleties and the area-law coefficient depend on dimension and field content.
artifact.status_search_result: The d=2 and d=4 de Sitter horizon cases have been computed (Surya–X.–Yazdi, CQG 2021, arXiv:2008.07697), where appropriate truncation of small Pauli–Jordan eigenvalues yields the expected area law matching the Gibbons–Hawking coefficient. A 2024 numerical follow-up (Phys. Rev. D 111, 065010, arXiv:2407.07811) further explores entanglement entropy in de Sitter. However, a general treatment for arbitrary spacetime dimensions and for field theories beyond the conformally coupled scalar, together with a fully principled (non-ad hoc) prescription for the small-eigenvalue truncation, has not been established, so the broader problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Entanglement Entropy of Causal Set de Sitter Horizons
status_evidence.snippet: SSEE obeys an area law when the spectrum of the Pauli–Jordan operator is appropriately truncated in both the de Sitter slab and its Rindler-like wedge; without truncation a volume law results.
status_evidence.claim: Area law for d=2,4 de Sitter horizons established after small-eigenvalue truncation.

status_evidence.title: Numerical calculation of entanglement entropy in de Sitter space
status_evidence.snippet: A 2024/25 numerical study of entanglement entropy in de Sitter space building on causal set methods.
status_evidence.claim: Recent follow-up work continues numerical investigation, indicating the program is active and not fully closed.

status_evidence.title: Everything You Always Wanted to Know About How Causal Set Theory Can Help with Open Questions in Cosmology
status_evidence.snippet: States that small-eigenvalue subtleties of i∆ need careful handling and that revisiting and extending to other dimensions/field theories would be interesting.
status_evidence.claim: Author identifies extensions as open directions.
